Could you please clarify what you mean by "brigading"?
Asking users on one or multiple subs to upvote/downvote/help clarify misunderstandings on (an)other sub(s).

I don't think it should be an issue - people are free to band together (the right to assemble) and do whatever they please. However, if we notice any concerted effort to manipulate Voat voting and other mechanisms, we will probably take action, but every case would have to be treated individually.

When there are conflicting ideologies at the same site, that's when things will eventually clash.

Let's say as a silly, fictional example that I hate dogs, and post my opinion on /v/doghaters (10 subscribers). Then /v/welovedogs (1000 subscribers) finds my opinion on dogs and link my comment on /v/welovedogs with the title "Get a load of this asshole!". Suddenly my submission is downvoated into hell and back, along with a few other posts from /v/doghaters, just because we had a different opinion than a larger community.

That raises the question, should bigger communities be allowed to affect smaller ones in that way? Should there be subverse-specific rules on how many comment points you need to have before you are allowed to downvoat?

We could implement a subverse setting where subverse owners could set ratios/quotas on who can vote and how much. Account age, CCP earned in that sub, max # of votes a comment can get, vote-aging etc. But I'm afraid these will have to wait until we get some other, more pressing features ready. For example, I'd love to see v2 (sets) layout fully implemented first. We'll figure something out :)

Limiting downvoats based on CCP/comment points earned in that sub might be the best tool against brigading. Also possibly a way for at least the mods to see if a comment/submission was linked to from another subverse. I think somebody built a bot for it in Reddit. I'm fairly sure it'll happen here as well if it becomes a problem.

And yeah, no need to worry about these features yet though. These issues won't become relevant until the userbase grows a bit more. The site is working pretty well for it's size right now. :)
